verdict.desc: Monday's historic Nvidia-fueled melt-up has fully reversed. Overnight a Reuters report that the White House could slap new tariffs on 16 trading partners collided with a deepening AI/chip selloff, and S&P 500 futures fell ~1.9%, Nasdaq-100 futures ~2.8–3% with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq on track for their worst November since 2008. The VIX jumped back above 30 — the VIX volatility index jumped 14.6% to 30.26, its highest level since the 35.89 close on November 20. Composite gap-risk sits at 76 (HOT) and P(≥1% gap) is ~49%, well above the 35% trigger, so GREEN is locked out. On top of that, October PCE drops at 8:30 ET and CME FedWatch assigned a 97.8% probability to a quarter-point Fed hike on December 9. The scanner boarded one Type-A bear call (AMBA, −35% on a guidance cut) — but it carries thin, unverified liquidity. Sell little or nothing new today.

focus.jnote: Monday's one-day melt-up is gone — a tariff headline plus an AI/chip rout has flipped the tape risk-off into October PCE and a holiday-thin week. Tuesday the market already faded: 7,201.09 was Tuesday's S&P 500 close, −0.50%; the Nasdaq Composite fell 1.48% to 23,733.54 and the Dow rose 0.85% to 50,018.70. Overnight it worsened: Nasdaq 100 futures were −3.03% and S&P 500 futures −2.02% at 7:21am ET as chip and AI stocks extended losses and a Reuters report said the White House could put new duties on 16 trading partners. By mid-morning S&P 500 futures fell to 7,078.50, down 139.00 points, or 1.93%, as of 7:40 a.m. New York time. The fear gauge re-expanded hard: the VIX jumped 14.6% to 30.26, its highest level since the 35.89 close on November 20. A Sniper does not sell premium into a tariff-shock, VIX-above-30 tape with a major inflation print due at 8:30 — cash is a position today.
focus.notdown: There is no clean bullish 'Not-Down' name today. The one boarded setup (AMBA) is a bearish bear-call, and the entire tape is risk-off: the three major US index futures fell in unison, with Dow futures down 1.20%, S&P 500 futures down 1.89% and Nasdaq futures down 2.86%. Selling bull puts into a deepening AI/chip rout with a Dec 9 hike nearly locked is a knife-catch, not a Sniper edge. The disciplined answer on the bull side is to sell nothing new today.
focus.notup: AMBA is the only boarded 'Not-Up' lean — a bear call on a shattered guidance print — but it is thin and unverified. Ambarella fell about 35% premarket after Q3 revenue of $115.2M missed and Q4 guidance of $70M to $75M blamed the memory shortage on customers, and Morgan Stanley downgraded the stock and BofA moved to Underperform. The catalyst is genuinely bearish and durable, but the scanner itself flags zero open interest, a one-sided ATM market and no S/R layers below — so even this is treat-as-illiquid. On a RED day, selling bear calls into a VIX>30, holiday-thin tape with squeeze risk on any relief bounce is not a table-pounder.
focus.why: Why RED? Four things stack. One: composite 76 is HOT and P(≥1% gap) at ~49% is well above the 35% trigger — either alone locks out GREEN. Two: a tariff headline on 16 trade partners plus a deepening AI/chip selloff has fully unwound Monday's melt-up, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq on track for their worst November since 2008. Three: October PCE prints at 8:30 ET — a scheduled inflation release inside the next 24h that by itself forbids GREEN — with a 97.8% probability of a quarter-point Fed hike on December 9 and thin holiday liquidity that amplifies any move. Four: the lone boarded name (AMBA) has unverified, thin liquidity. Stand down on new credit spreads, or push DTE past the Dec 9 FOMC and cut size hard. Cash is a position today.

setups.read: Boarded Grade A, bearish — copied verbatim — but read the fine print before touching it. The catalyst is real and durable: Ambarella reported EPS of 28 cents, missing the 32-cent consensus, and revenue of $115.22 million fell short of the $119.44 million estimate. The killer was guidance: Ambarella guided fiscal fourth-quarter revenue to $70 million to $75 million, roughly 37% below the quarter it just reported, blaming the memory shortage, and Morgan Stanley downgraded the stock and BofA moved to Underperform. The stock is gapping hard: shares dipped 36.7% to $28.17 in pre-market trading. But the scanner's own flags are disqualifying for premium-selling: open interest 0 (below the 500 bar), a one-sided/unquoted ATM market (treat as illiquid), reaction volume only 0.40× (below the 1.3× bar), and NO S/R layers within 7% — nothing between price and the short strike. Note too the scanner's next-earnings field reads 2027-02-23, outside any DTE, which is fine — but liquidity, not timing, is the problem here.

risks: New tariff shock — a Reuters report says the White House could put new duties on imports from 16 trading partners, which drove the overnight risk-off. Any confirmation or escalation gaps the whole tape; this is the number-one thing to watch.

October PCE at 8:30 ET — the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, with PCE likely up 0.3% M/M, core PCE seen rising 3.2% Y/Y vs 3.1% prior, and core PCE up 0.3% M/M. A hot print feeds more-hikes fear directly into a fragile tape.
AI / chip concentration — NVDA traded ~$147.35 pre-market against a $155.38 Tuesday close. A single-name AI reversal is driving the index; one more leg down in chips drags the whole market with it.

Dec 9 Fed hike ~97% priced — CME FedWatch assigned a 97.8% probability to a quarter-point hike on December 9, with a 2.2% chance of no change. A rate backdrop tightening into a correcting tape caps any relief and pressures high-multiple tech.

Holiday-thin liquidity — US markets are closed Thursday and reopen for a shortened Friday session; with fewer orders, relatively small flows could trigger substantial price swings, break key technical levels and prompt stop-loss cascades. This is the week's biggest tail.
